name: Kabiye
notes: Kabiye (Kabɩyɛ) of Togo, written in a Latin orthography based on the African reference alphabet, in which most letters are the IPA symbol of the phoneme they write (ɖ, ɩ, ʊ, ɛ, ɔ, ŋ). ⟨c⟩=/tʃ/, ⟨j⟩=/dʒ/, ⟨ñ⟩=/ɲ/, ⟨y⟩=/j/; ⟨kp⟩ and ⟨gb⟩ are labial-velar stops. Long vowels are written doubled, which the map handles as a sequence of two identical vowels. Kabiye has two tones (H, L) with automatic downstep; tone is not marked in the standard orthography, so no tone marks are emitted. ATR vowel harmony pairs ɩ/i, ʊ/u, ɛ/e, ɔ/o.

sources.notes: Consonant chart with a spelled word per phoneme (pp. 215-216) and the vowel section (p. 218), read in full. It states the orthography's departures from the IPA outright: tʃ dʒ ɲ j ɖ are written ⟨c j ñ y ɖ⟩, which is what this map has, and the labial-velars ⟨kp gb⟩ are k͡p ɡ͡b. Nine vowel qualities in two tongue-root sets, i ɪ u ʊ e ɛ o ɔ a, long vowels written by doubling, tone unwritten; all as mapped. Two points against the map: ⟨r⟩ is an allophone of /ɖ/ confined to ideophones, not a phoneme, and ⟨ŋ⟩ is the coda variant of /n/ or /ɲ/, not a separate phoneme; the source also lists a velarisation graph ⟨G⟩ that the map does not read. Recorded here, not changed.
